pr_title: Add start time timestamps to `<testcase>`/Run data in JUnit XML output from `terraform test`
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/36296

This PR adds `timestamp` attributes to the `<testcase>` elements in the JUnit format XML output for `terraform test`.

I'm implementing testing for this feature (JUnit format output in general) in a separate PR, but wanted to keep this new addition separate from that work.

Here is an example of the XML output following this PR:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><testsuites>
  <testsuite name="example_1.tftest.hcl" tests="1" skipped="0" failures="0" errors="0">
    <testcase name="true_is_true" classname="example_1.tftest.hcl" time="0.00325975" timestamp="2025-01-08T16:00:44Z"></testcase>
  </testsuite>
  <testsuite name="example_2.tftest.hcl" tests="1" skipped="0" failures="1" errors="0">
    <testcase name="false_is_false" classname="example_2.tftest.hcl" time="0.001073916" timestamp="2025-01-08T16:00:44Z">
      <failure message="Test run failed"></failure>
      <system-err><![CDATA[
Error: Test assertion failed

  on example_2.tftest.hcl line 21:
  (source code not available)

local.false did not match expected value
]]></system-err>
    </testcase>
  </testsuite>
</testsuites>
```

Note: these tests are trivial tests that make assertions about local values, so the timestamps are the same. If a test was using providers to interact with third parties then the timestamps would be more distinct.

pr_comments: Note to reviewers: I've used [this resource as a reference](https://github.com/testmoapp/junitxml?tab=readme-ov-file#complete-junit-xml-example) for the JUnit XML format and I've chosen to only add the attribute to the place it was requested for. It's possible to add `time` and `timestamp` attrs to several elements, but I think it'd be worth waiting for those to be requested if they're useful

issue_context.title: Add `timestamp` attributes to JUnit XML formatted output from `terraform test`
issue_context.body:
### Terraform Version

```shell
Terraform v1.10.0
on darwin_arm64
```


### Use Cases

[From a response](https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/request-for-feedback-on-terraform-test-junit-xml-output/62307/22?u=sarah.french) in the Discuss forum thread Request for Feedback on Terraform Test JUnit XML output:

> Is it possible to add timestamp attributes for test cases?
Some reporting tools uses them to show when test have ran.

### Attempted Solutions

N/A

### Proposal

Add `timestamp` attributes to the `<testcase>` elements that represent run blocks in .tf.test.hcl files

### References

- https://discuss.hashicorp.com/t/request-for-feedback-on-terraform-test-junit-xml-output/62307/

review_comments: If this code is hit (`Start` is never set to a non-zero value) then the resulting XML will completely exclude the `timestamp` attribute instead of using the empty string. The alternative would be to have timestamp attribute present but set to `"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"`

It seems the time here is in local time. Should we set the time to UTC? There doesn't seem to be a specified format in the standards,  but if the timezone is not specified, then UTC makes it easier for multiple people to work with the same test output. I dont know how often that happens for terraform users though. What do you think?
Thanks, I overlooked that- resolved in [b5cc74e](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/pull/36295/commits/b5cc74e0e7fe644457998f10a4cbcda0bb185248)
